title: Concentrate an ideal-power product on a closed subset
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], F a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], K quasi-coherent ideal sheaf data, and C a closed subset. If the nonzero-stalk locus of F [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is contained in the union of the zero set of K and C, there is a nonnegative integer n for which the ideal power K^n is quasi-coherent and the nonzero-stalk locus of K^n F is contained in C. Powers and products are the recursively constructed sheaf powers and multiplication images of lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk. This asserts no coherence of the product or quotient, no exact sequence, and no strict support bound.

source.place: Tag 01YD, proof of Lemma 30.12.1 on the Noetherian complement of the second closed set; Tag 01Y9, Lemma 30.10.2; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YD

proof.text: Use isCoherent_iff_isQuasicoherent_and_isFiniteType to obtain quasi-coherence and finite type of F. Let V be the complement of C. NoetherianSpace.isCompact and isCompact_and_isOpen_iff_finite_and_eq_biUnion_affineOpens give a finite set S of affine opens of X with union V. Every member of S is contained in V. This avoids restricting F or constructing a Noetherian open subscheme.

For each U in S, finite_type_module_support_closed identifies the nonzero-stalk locus intersected with U with the image of V(Ann Gamma(F,U)) in X. The support hypothesis and U subset V put this locus in K.support. Mathlib IdealSheafData.coe_support_inter and IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_image_zeroLocus identify K.support intersected with U with the image of V(K.ideal U). Injectivity of fromSpec gives the zero-locus containment. PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_subset_zeroLocus_iff gives K.ideal U subset radical(Ann Gamma(F,U)). The affine ring is Noetherian; apply Ideal.exists_pow_le_of_le_radical_of_fg to get an exponent. Choose the finite supremum t of these exponents. Ideal.pow_le_pow_right shows that K.ideal U raised to t annihilates Gamma(F,U) for every U in S.

Reuse the proved general private helpers of CoherentSupportVanishingIdealNilpotence through import all: ideal_qc shows that K.toModules is quasi-coherent, and powers_affine_sections proves quasi-coherence of all recursive powers and identifies the affine range of the inclusion with K.ideal U raised to t. Quasi-coherent tensor and image results prove quasi-coherence of H = K^t F. multiplication_range identifies the affine range of H into F with K.ideal U raised to t times Gamma(F,U). The annihilator bound makes that submodule zero. Monicity of the image inclusion gives injectivity on sections, so Gamma(H,U) is subsingleton for each U in S.

For x outside C choose U in S containing x. The proved affine_source_zero_of_sections helper of CoherentSupportVanishingIdealNilpotence makes H restricted to U a zero object. Apply moduleStalkFunctor to obtain a subsingleton stalk there. Mathlib restrictStalkNatIso identifies that stalk with H_x, proving the support inclusion. If V is empty the empty cover gives t = 0; powers_affine_sections includes exponent zero. The unit record has no realized statement or step carried by any of the bypassed node-level lemmas.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01YD support-concentration step and Tag 01Y9, implemented directly on a finite affine cover of the complement. General affine helpers reused from the proved vanishing-ideal nilpotence module to avoid the cyclic ideal-times and restriction packages.

lean.statement:
theorem coherent_ideal_power_supported_on_closed
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F)
    (K : X.IdealSheafData) (C : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X)
    (hSupp : {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆
      (K.support : Set X) ∪ (C : Set X)) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, (idealSheafPower K.toModulesι n).1.IsQuasicoherent ∧
      {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton
        ((idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower K.toModulesι n).2 F).presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆
        (C : Set X)
